correctness.rationale: The proof constructs the polar in the exact ambient zero-sum Euclidean hyperplane; shows every vertex has a tight spanning tree and integer values 0..3 (graph diameter 3); exhausts range-3 missing-matching potentials of squared norm (n+8)/2, full-biclique range<=2 potentials with maximum n-(n mod 2)/(2n), and remaining range-2 diagonal-gap potentials with norm at most n/2+2. These disjoint exhaustive possibilities give the exact squared circumradius and equality families, including the n=8 tie. By polarity and central symmetry this is the global insphere radius; strict convexity and vertex-facet duality give exact tangent counts. Exact rational tests n=3..14 and direct-coordinate tests n=3,4 passed, but the proof, not tests, supplies the infinite quantifier.

value.rationale: The crown graph K_{n,n} minus its matched edges is a natural sharply structured bipartite double cover of the complete graph. Removing a perfect matching generates graph-distance-three polar potentials that compete exactly with balanced complete-bipartite cut potentials. The theorem gives a natural intrinsic Euclidean invariant for infinitely many polytope dimensions, the unique sharp changeover n=8, and a full characterization and exact count of nearest facets (not just a computed bound). This is a structural geometric transition, not a routine numerical slice, and may inform graph-spread and symmetric-edge-polytope metric studies.
